cases.expected: Iterator returned by AXFR() has no elements; hasNext() returns false and next() throws NoSuchElementException.
cases.description: Verify that AXFR() on a freshly created Zone with no RRsets returns an iterator that correctly reports an empty collection.

cases.expected: Iterator returns exactly one RRset (the one added) and then hasNext() returns false.
cases.description: Add a single RRset (e.g., an A record for www.example.com) to the Zone, call AXFR() and ensure the iterator yields that RRset and then terminates.

cases.expected: Iterator yields all added RRsets in the order defined by ZoneIterator (typically lexical order of names, then type). The number of elements returned equals the number of RRsets added.
cases.description: Populate the Zone with several RRsets (A, AAAA, MX, NS) for different names, invoke AXFR() and verify that the iterator traverses every RRset exactly once and respects the expected ordering.

cases.expected: Two consecutive calls to AXFR() return two distinct iterator instances; advancing one iterator does not affect the other.
cases.description: Create a Zone with a few RRsets, obtain iterator1 = zone.AXFR(), then iterator2 = zone.AXFR(). Advance iterator1 one step and confirm iterator2 still starts at the first element.

group: AXFR iterator type and unsupported operations

cases.expected: The object returned by AXFR() is an instance of Zone.ZoneIterator (or a subclass) and its remove() method throws UnsupportedOperationException.
cases.description: Check the runtime type of the iterator returned by AXFR() and verify that calling remove() on it results in an UnsupportedOperationException, as ZoneIterator is read‑only.

group: AXFR ordering by name and type

cases.expected: Iterator returns RRsets in lexical order of names, and for identical names in ascending order of type numeric value (e.g., A (1) before AAAA (28)). For a zone containing RRsets: A record for b.example.com, AAAA record for a.example.com, MX record for a.example.com, the iterator yields: AAAA(a.example.com), MX(a.example.com), A(b.example.com).
cases.description: Verify that ZoneIterator sorts RRsets first by the fully‑qualified name (lexicographically) and then by the DNS type code, ensuring deterministic AXFR ordering.

cases.expected: When two RRsets share the same name but different types (e.g., A and AAAA for www.example.com), the iterator yields the lower type number first (A before AAAA).
cases.description: Confirm that for identical names the iterator respects type ordering rather than insertion order.

group: AXFR iterator throws ConcurrentModificationException after zone modification

cases.expected: ConcurrentModificationException thrown when calling next() on the iterator after adding a new RRset to the Zone.
cases.description: Obtain an iterator via zone.AXFR(), then add an additional RRset to the same Zone before invoking iterator.next(). The iterator should detect the structural change and raise ConcurrentModificationException.

group: AXFR iterator throws NullPointerException when a null RRset is present

cases.expected: NullPointerException thrown during iteration when the Zone contains a null RRset entry.
cases.description: Directly insert a null RRset into the Zone's internal storage (e.g., via reflection or a specially crafted addRRset(null) if the method permits null). Calling zone.AXFR() and then iterator.next() should encounter the null entry and raise NullPointerException.

group: AXFR iterator throws IllegalStateException after iterator is exhausted and next() called again

cases.expected: IllegalStateException thrown when next() is invoked on an iterator that has already reached the end of the collection.
cases.description: Iterate over all RRsets returned by zone.AXFR() until hasNext() returns false. Call iterator.next() once more; the iterator should signal that it is in an illegal state and throw IllegalStateException (different from NoSuchElementException which is thrown on a fresh empty iterator).
